summary: The publisher retraction marker at the start of a title is followed either by a colon or bracket, or by a spaced dash; the dash counts only directly after the marker word or after one singular noun from a closed list (article, paper, publication, manuscript, chapter), with whitespace on both sides, so ordinary titles that merely start with the word stay unmarked.
reason: Some publishers write "Retracted Paper - <title>" or "RETRACTED – <title>". The colon/bracket rule left those works in the softer index-only tier, or unmarked when the index flag is missing, while a free window before any dash would mark titles such as "Withdrawn patients - outcomes ...". A regen that rebuilds the pattern must keep both separators and the noun limit.
validated_outcome: On a 1,490-title OpenAlex sample the dash rule changed only dash-marker titles and added no non-marker. TestDetectRetractionDashSeparator kills seven pattern mutations that the existing retraction tests all pass; TestKnownGapSingularNounAboutRetraction records the accepted cost.
